meta.description: Best-known PROVEN lower bounds for s(n), the side of the smallest square that can contain n non-overlapping axis-free unit squares, for n=1..324.
meta.caveats: See site/notes/lower-bounds-notes.md for sourcing notes and uncertainties. Entries with status 'preprint' are 2026 results that have not been refereed (most computer-assisted; Karakus 2026 is a conventional arXiv proof). Others' certificates are linked as published; this project replays only its own. Where a 2026 repository is still moving (n = 17 especially), the history keeps the main steps and the linked repository has the rest.
meta.precision: `value` is the full double-precision evaluation of `exact_form`, not a rounded decimal: storing the n=5 floor as 2.7071068 put it ABOVE the true 2+1/sqrt(2)=2.707106781..., so it compared as greater than the matching upper bound and s(5) and s(10) were reported open with a gap of -0.0000. Entries whose exact_form is absent or flagged unreliable keep their curated decimal.
meta.families: s(k^2-3) = k is proved here for every k >= 6 (EvanDaniel2026, 2026-09-29, s12/certificates/k2m3). The table covers n <= 100, so it holds the cases n = 33, 46, 61, 78, 97 (k = 6..10); for n = 33, 46, 61, which were already settled, it is a history entry and `best` keeps the earlier proof; for n = 78, 97 it is `best`. The family continues beyond the table (n = 118, 141, ...). s(k^2-4) = k is proved here for every k >= 5 (EvanDaniel2026, 2026-10-03, s12/certificates/k2m4): for k >= 8 by one family (its 9 x 9 box certified by our exact checker and, for the tilted squares, re-checked by wand125's separately written exact checker (2026-10-06; reviewed by jlevy/squares, recorded there as reported evidence, T-081 not yet register-verified), the box-to-every-k reduction in Lean), for k = 5, 6, 7 by the separate s21, s32, s45 bundles, which are the entries for n = 21, 32, 45. In the table: n = 60 (k = 8) gets a history entry and `best` keeps the s60 bundle; n = 77 (k = 9) is `best`, with wand125's earlier s(77) = 9 (2026-10-01) in the history; n = 96 (k = 10) is `best`. The family continues beyond the table (n = 117, 140, ...).
meta.reported: Entries with "reported": true are values their authors report but that no one other than the author has replayed (jlevy/squares grades them V0/C0). They are kept in `history` for the record and are never `best`, even where they are larger.
meta.claimed: Entries with status "claimed" are values whose proof was never published and cannot be reviewed: T. Green's 2000 bounds, cited in Friedman's survey DS7 as a private communication (Theorems 9-10 and Table 2), and Friedman's table values for n = 13 (3.8437) and n = 21 (4.7438), which the survey gives without figure or proof. They are kept in the history for the record and are never `best`. For n = 17-18 the survey's Figure 34 draws Green's unavoidable set, which could be checked; it has not been checked here.
meta.gap: Entries with status "gap" are published results whose published proof is known to be incomplete: Nagamochi 2005 (Theorem 2, both the k^2-1 / k^2-2 families and the general bound) rests on his Lemma 1, which is false (chelokot 2026, a Lean-checked counterexample; H. Karakus, arXiv:2609.37410, a family of counterexamples). The statements are not disproved. They are kept in the history and are never best. s(k^2-1) = k is re-proved by Karakus 2026 and s(k^2-2) = k by chelokot 2026 (Lean); Karakus's weaker general bound 1/2 + sqrt(N - floor(sqrt N) + 1/4) has a complete proof and is listed for every nonsquare N >= 8.
meta.register: `register: verified` on a 2026 `best`: jlevy/squares' register lists that floor for n as verified (checked 2026-10-07). The Overview marks these n as proved, with a ring rather than a dot (unrefereed). n = 96 = 10^2 - 4 is not marked: there our s = 10 is registered as reported (T-081, full replay running).
